Definition: i.e. G1437 and G3361; if not, i.e. unless:--X before, but, except, if, no, (if, + whosoever) not.
BiblicalUsage: If not, unless, the two-word phrase that sets the condition, as in except your righteousness exceed the righteousness of the scribes, or except a man be born of water and of the Spirit. The words never stand as one word in the Greek text; they are two words working as one condition.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the unless of Jesus is the narrow door of the kingdom, because except we turn and become as little children, we shall not enter in.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
